name: Inside the GeForce RTX 5070 Ti
subtitle: From the whole MSI card down to the GB203 die: 45.6 billion transistors on 378 mm² of silicon, fed by 8 memory chips and 300 W.
heading: Inside the
GeForce RTX 5070 Ti

finale.title: 70 of 84 SMs, switched on.
finale.text: The 5070 Ti enables 70 of the GB203's 84 streaming multiprocessors: 8,960 CUDA cores. Which ones are switched off varies from chip to chip.

levels.title: GeForce RTX 5070 Ti
levels.text: MSI Ventus 3X OC: 303 × 121 mm, three fans over a fin stack, 300 W board power.
levels.caption: Three fans, one chip, 300 watts.

levels.title: Main PCB
levels.text: The GB203 sits in the middle, ringed by 8 GDDR7 chips on a 256-bit bus (896 GB/s). Power enters at the 12V-2×6 connector and is stepped down for the core.
levels.caption: Power in, bytes out.

levels.title: GB203 package
levels.text: A flip-chip package: the die sits face-down on layers of copper wiring that fan its connections out to the solder balls underneath.
levels.caption: Fanning out thousands of connections.

levels.title: GB203 die
levels.text: TSMC 4N, 378 mm², 45.6 billion transistors: 7 GPCs around 64 MB of L2 cache, with memory controllers on the edges.
levels.caption: Where the work happens.
